name: Cottage pie
summary: Savoury beef mince with carrots and peas under a buttery mashed potato lid, baked until the forked ridges turn golden.
about: Cottage pie came to South Africa with British home cooking and became a weeknight standby: one dish, mince that stretches, and a crisp potato top children fight over. Many families stir a little chutney or Worcestershire sauce into the mince and finish the mash with grated cheese.
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot of cold salted water, bring to the boil and cook for 18–20 minutes, until a knife slides through them easily.
While they cook, heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and fry the onion and carrots for 6–8 minutes, until the onion is soft. Add the garlic and fry for 1 minute.
Turn the heat up to high, add the mince and fry for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until no pink remains and the liquid has cooked away.

Stir in the tomato paste, herbs, Worcestershire sauce, chutney and stock. Simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and saucy rather than wet. Stir in the peas and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C for a fan oven). Drain the potatoes well and mash them with the butter and warm milk until smooth, then season with salt.

Spoon the mince into a 2-litre ovenproof dish. Dollop the mash over and spread it to the edges to seal in the filling, then rough up the top with a fork. Dot with the extra butter and scatter over the cheese, if using.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the filling bubbles at the edges and the ridges of the potato are golden brown. Rest for 5 minutes before serving with extra peas or a green salad.
prepNote: Assemble up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge; bake 10 minutes longer from cold.
